When did anti-Zionism emerge as a distin.question: When did anti-Zionism emerge as a distinct position?
When did anti-Zionism emerge as a distin.answer: Anti-Zionism emerged as opposition existed from the beginning, alongside Theodor Herzl's call for a Jewish state, with the term shifting meaning after 1948 when Israel was established.
When did anti-Zionism emerge as a distin.value: from the late 19th century (Herzl era), shifting focus after 1948
When did anti-Zionism emerge as a distin.evidence: From the beginning, there was resistance to Zionism and Theodor Herzl's call for the establishment of a Jewish state in Palestine.

Which religious and political groups doe.answer: The article names Orthodox rabbis, assimilationist Jewish liberals, left-wing Jewish movements like the Bund and Autonomists, Reform rabbis, Agudat Yisrael, the Yevsektsiya, Moroccan Sephardic communities, the Jewish Anti-Zionist League in Egypt, the American Council for Judaism, some Haredi Jews, and Arab/Palestinian groups.
Which religious and political groups doe.value: Orthodox rabbis, Bund, Autonomists, Reform rabbis, Agudat Yisrael, Yevsektsiya, Moroccan Jewish communities, Jewish Anti-Zionist League, American Council for Judaism, Haredi Jews, Palestinians/Arabs
Which religious and political groups doe.evidence: Opposition came from diverse sources: many Orthodox rabbis held that a Jewish state before the messiah was against divine will; assimilationist Jewish liberals feared Zionism threatened efforts at integration and citizenship in European states; and various left-wing Jewish movements, such as the Bund and Autonomists, promoted alternative forms of Jewish identity... more traditionalist groups like Agudat Yisrael opposed cooperation with secular Zionists... In Egypt in 1946, Jewish members of Iskra, an underground Communist movement, founded the Jewish Anti-Zionist League... some, including the American Council for Judaism, continued to oppose the ideology... Some are anti-Zionist for religious reasons, such as some Haredi Jews.

When did anti-Zionism emerge as a distin.answer: Not explicitly dated as a distinct term; the article's first reference point is the March 1920 large-scale anti-Zionist demonstrations in Palestine, and Orthodox Jewish rejection is linked to the rise of the Orthodox trend as a reaction to the Reform movement in the first half of the 19th century.
When did anti-Zionism emerge as a distin.value: first half of 19th century (Orthodox Jewish rejection); March 1920 (first large demonstrations in Palestine)

adjudication.question: When did anti-Zionism emerge as a distinct position?
adjudication.note: All place origins in 19th century/early Zionist era, but en/he emphasize Herzl-era Jewish debates while ar emphasizes Orthodox rejection and 1920 Palestine demonstrations.

adjudication.question: Which religious and political groups does the article identify as holding anti-Zionist positions?
adjudication.note: Each edition lists a different, only partially overlapping set of groups (en: mostly Jewish political/religious groups plus Palestinians; he: Jewish factions plus post-Zionist/left/Islamist/neo-Nazi; ar: mainly Arab/Islamic states and organizations plus Neturei Karta), reflecting differing emphasis rather than outright contradiction.
